messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: log_prob [w/o dropping constants]
parts:
If you want to do that, you need to replace every
statement of the form

y ~ foo(theta);

with

increment_log_prob(foo_log(y,theta));

The code generated for a program has a template parameter
propto__ on the log_prob function that if set to false will
keep everything --- we need to get that plumbed through
the calls to allow it as an option at the top level.

- Bob

> On Mar 10, 2015, at 2:00 PM, Jiqiang Guo <guo...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I think the answer is no as the model does not have this option. In fact, as a user of the model class translated by stanc, even whether the constant is drop or not is unknown. For example, we don't know if the user uses normal_log function or ~ normal notation.
>
> I am cc-ing Bob in case I am wrong or there is change in Stan.
>
> Jiqiang
>
> On Mon, Mar 9, 2015 at 10:42 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
> For a stanfit object, is it possible to obtain the log-posterior without dropping constants in the log-likelihood and log-priors but with the Jacobian adjustment?
>

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: log_prob [w/o dropping constants]
parts:
So I was kind of wrong.  Suppose we only have y ~ foo(theta) in the model specification.  Do you (Bob) imply that it's not plumbed through though on the top level there is such functionality?  

But anyway, in current rstan, log_prob_propto in https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/blob/develop/src/stan/model/util.hpp is used.  So there is no option for now. 

Jiqiang
